title: Judge a synthetic voice by register
statement: Judge a narration voice by its register and pace rather than by whether it is synthetic, since modern synthetic voices taught adults as well as recorded human ones.
detail: The Grade 9 research brief, from abstracts and a summary, reports that a modern text-to-speech engine matched a recorded human voice on learning and credibility ratings and beat an older engine on transfer and efficiency, and that a 2019 follow-up found modern synthetic speech not statistically different from a human voice on perceptions, learning or efficiency. Both studies used adult online samples. The brief concludes that the risk lies in register, not in the voice being synthetic, and asks for a peer-adult register at normal speech rate, with no sing-song or exclamatory praise.
against: The same brief gives a human voice a median d = 0.8 under the voice principle, and it found no controlled study of synthetic-voice register or pace for 14–15-year-olds (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/learners-voice-guide.md`, lines 64 and 92), so the rule is untested with children and teens.

evidence.quote: A modern TTS engine matched a recorded human voice on learning and credibility ratings and beat an older engine on transfer and efficiency (Craig & Schroeder 2017).
A 2019 follow-up found modern TTS "not statistically different" from a human voice on perceptions, learning or efficiency.
Both studies used adult online samples.
The risk lies in register, not in the voice being synthetic.
Use a peer-adult register at normal speech rate, with no sing-song or exclamatory praise.
